claims.text: Increasing lattice distortion in a homogeneous, single-phase HEA enhances hardness and strength.
Lattice distortion raises the energy barriers for dislocation motion.
Higher lattice friction impedes dislocation slip and increases resistance to plastic deformation.
An FCC NiCoCr-based alloy can provide a concentrated, near-equiatomic baseline for the comparison.
Standard solution treatment or homogenization annealing can produce a uniform, phase-pure NiCoCr-based baseline with minimal lattice distortion.
Adding 2–5 at.% of an element with substantially different atomic radius will selectively increase lattice distortion.
The proposed 2–5 at.% addition can increase distortion without altering phase constitution or grain structure.
X-ray diffraction peak shifts and broadening can quantify the degree of local lattice distortion in these samples.
Transmission electron microscopy local-strain measurements can quantify the degree of local lattice distortion.
A rugged atomic energy landscape produces elevated lattice resistance to dislocation motion.
The intentionally induced lattice distortion is what creates the more rugged atomic energy landscape.
The modified alloy should have higher hardness than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy should have higher yield strength than the baseline alloy.
Hardness and yield-strength improvements should correlate quantitatively with the measured extent of induced lattice distortion when grain size and phase constitution are controlled.
Grain size and phase constitution must be controlled because they can independently affect mechanical behavior.
The proposed relationship is limited to single-phase, near-equiatomic HEAs whose grain size and phase distribution remain constant.
The strengthening effect may diminish or reverse if the compositional modification induces secondary phases, excessive strain, or amorphization.
Short-range ordering may contribute to strength independently of nominal lattice distortion.
The beneficial-distortion threshold before adverse effects occur is not established.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant increase in both hardness and yield strength, or failure to observe a distortion–property correlation, would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
